text.tspan: So Long, and Thanks for All the Seeds:

tspan.tspan: To replace classical public-key primitives (such as RSA and ECDSA) that are vulnerable
to Shor's algorithm on quantum architectures, the National Institute of Standards and
Technology (NIST) initiated a standardization competition to evaluate and

text.tspan: standardize secure post-quantum digital signature schemes.

tspan.tspan: To guarantee authenticity, integrity, and non-repudiation in a post-quantum setting,

text.tspan: several leading signature candidates rely on zero-knowledge (ZK) proof systems.

tspan.tspan: Prominent ZK-based constructions derive non-interactive digital signatures by
applying the Fiat-Shamir transformation to underlying interactive identification
protocols.Specifically, MEDS is a code-based post-quantum primitive whose
underlying security rests on the computational hardness of the Matrix Code

text.tspan: Equivalence (MCE) problem in the rank metric.

tspan.tspan: Unlike passive side-channel analysis that measures physical emissions like timing or
power consumption, fault-injection attacks actively disrupt physical hardware during
Adversaries apply physical stressors, such as clock glitches, voltage spikes, laser pulses,
or electromagnetic fields, to alter control flow, skip assembly instructions, corrupt

text.tspan: register values, or force early loop terminations.

tspan.tspan: In seed-tree-based ZK signatures, injecting physical perturbations during seed
publication can force the exposure of hidden ephemeral seeds alongside their
TWe choose to focus on clock

Zero-knowledge signature schemes require generating independent ephemeral
commitments across multiple parallel execution rounds, each of which must be
driven by an isolated random seed so that disclosing the randomness of public round

text.tspan: does not leak information about hidden, secret-dependent rounds.

tspan.tspan: Transmitting large numbers of independent random seeds individually within every

text.tspan: signature produces large signature payload sizes.

tspan.tspan: To minimize payload size, schemes deploy Goldreich-Goldwasser-Micali (GGM)
binary trees to expand a single master root seed into all required leaf seeds via top-
The signer transmits the minimal set of intermediate co-path nodes (seed path)

text.tspan: required for the verifier to recompute public leaf seeds.

tspan.tspan: A fault model defines the targetted position in the code, the precise timing, and

text.tspan: architectural effect of a physical disturbance on cryptographic software logic.
